title: Go: Authentication System
description: Build a complete authentication system in Go with JWT tokens, HMAC signing, password hashing, and role-based access control.

steps.title: HMAC signing utility
steps.description: Write a `signHMAC` function that takes a message string and a secret key, computes the HMAC-SHA256 using `crypto/hmac` and `crypto/sha256`, and returns the hex-encoded signature. Print the signature for the message "hello" with secret "mysecret".
hints: Use `hmac.New(sha256.New, []byte(secret))` to create the HMAC hasher
Write the message with `h.Write([]byte(message))` then call `h.Sum(nil)`

verification.successMessage: HMAC-SHA256 produces a consistent hex signature for a given message and key!
verification.failureMessage: Print the hex-encoded HMAC-SHA256 signature using fmt.Println.

steps.title: JWT header and payload encoding
steps.description: Implement a `base64URLEncode` helper and functions to build JWT segments. Build a JSON header `{"alg":"HS256","typ":"JWT"}` and a payload with `sub`, `iat`, and `exp` claims using `time.Now()`. Base64url-encode both and print the encoded header and payload.
hints: Use `encoding/json.Marshal` to serialize the header and payload structs to JSON

verification.successMessage: JWT header and payload are correctly JSON-encoded and base64url-encoded!
verification.failureMessage: Print the base64url-encoded header and payload separately using fmt.Println.

steps.title: JWT token generation and verification
steps.description: Combine previous steps into a `generateToken` function that returns a full JWT string (header.payload.signature). Write a `verifyToken` function that splits the token, recomputes the HMAC, and compares signatures using `hmac.Equal`. Print the generated token and the decoded payload from verification.
hints: Use `strings.Split(token, ".")` to get the three segments
Recompute signature on `segments[0] + "." + segments[1]` and compare with `hmac.Equal`

verification.successMessage: JWT generation and verification work correctly with HMAC-SHA256!
verification.failureMessage: Print the generated JWT token and the decoded payload after verification.

steps.title: Role-based access middleware
steps.description: Write a `RequireRole` function that takes allowed roles and returns a middleware function. The middleware checks a user's role from context and prints "Access granted" or "Access denied". Create users with different roles and test access to an "admin" endpoint. Use a simple map as a mock context.
hints: Define a `type Middleware func(map[string]string) bool` that takes a context map
`RequireRole` is a higher-order function: `func RequireRole(roles ...string) Middleware`
Test with at least three roles: "admin" (granted), "user" (denied), "guest" (denied)

verification.successMessage: Role-based middleware correctly gates access based on user role!
verification.failureMessage: Print 'Access granted' for admin and 'Access denied' for guest role.

steps.title: Complete login handler
steps.description: Combine all components into a `Login` function. It takes a username and password, looks up the user in a mock store (map with hashed passwords and roles), verifies the password, generates a JWT, and returns it. Print the generated token on success or "Invalid credentials" on failure.
hints: Store users as a `map[string]User` where User has Username, PasswordHash, Role fields
For password verification, re-HMAC the input password with the stored salt and compare
On successful login, call `generateToken` with the username and role in claims

verification.successMessage: Complete login flow works — valid credentials return a JWT, invalid ones are rejected!
verification.failureMessage: Print the JWT token for a valid login and 'Invalid credentials' for a failed one.
